The problem is that the validation character set `b"0123456789abcdefABCDEFghijklGHIJKL \t"` includes spaces and tabs, which means that chunk sizes like `0 ` (with trailing space) or ` 0` (with leading space) will pass validation, but they shouldn't according to the HTTP spec.

According to RFC 9112 Section 7.1:

chunk      = chunk-size [ chunk-ext ] CRLF chunk-data CRLF

The chunk-size must be one or more hex digits. Optional whitespace (BWS) is only allowed before chunk extensions (after a semicolon), not in the chunk-size itself.
